title: Telegram Bot API: Rate Limits, File Sizes, Errors
summary: Telegram Bot API is free and runs on HTTP at api.telegram.org. Register with BotFather for a token, and any server can send bot messages via HTTPS.
body_markdown:
## Call the same Telegram endpoints without code in Activepieces


In Activepieces, the Telegram Bot connector wraps the same Bot API methods and uses the same BotFather token, and using it is entirely optional; the curl calls above do the same job.


A no-code flow is therefore subject to every limit and failure mode above, including flood control, webhook rules and message size. The builder doesn't remove any of them.


The connector is one of the 746 integrations in` packages/pieces/community` in the MIT-licensed open source repository, so the Bot API methods it wraps can be read in its public source, next to the rest of the community integrations.


### Connect the token


Paste the token BotFather gave you into a new Telegram Bot connection, and the flow now acts as that bot. Nothing else is needed, because the Bot API is token-only.


In Activepieces the token is held centrally as a connection rather than pasted into each flow, and custom RBAC governs who can use it. Treat it as a secret either way.


If you rotate the token in BotFather, the old connection starts failing, so update it there too.


### Send and receive without code


For incoming updates the connector offers triggers, and for sending messages it offers actions. Where it has no dedicated action for a method, an HTTP action can call the Bot API endpoint directly with your token, which is useful for methods the connector doesn't wrap.


### Reading the example workflow


In the screenshot you can see the shape of a typical flow, here built on Discord rather than Telegram.


It's a "Community Summarizer - Get Messages" flow with a New Message trigger, a Create Record step, an AI "Needs Help?" check, a Router, and a Send Message step.


On the right panel you'll find the trigger's Connection, Limit and Channel fields, and the unpublished-changes notice at the top is a reminder that edits do nothing until you press Publish. Swap in the Telegram trigger and send action and the structure carries over.


### Handling failed sends


Next, treat the flow as you would code: check what happens when a send fails. A Router branch that handles an error response, such as a rate limit, is where the retry logic you would write by hand has to live.


### When to use code for Telegram bots


For high-volume broadcast, stay in code. There you need control over pacing, per-chat backoff, and honoring the retry delay Telegram returns, and a visual flow gives you less room to enforce that.


A flow suits low-volume replies, notifications and AI-assisted triage, where one message per event keeps you well inside the limits.
